claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

Please note this doesn't include higher education (like university) or paid employment/training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's actually just started an apprenticeship in England - he's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask a bit more about Alex's apprenticeship to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship a paid apprenticeship (where he receives a wage from an employer), or is it an unpaid traineeship?**

This distinction is important because paid apprenticeships are treated differently from unpaid traineeships when it comes to Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a paid apprenticeship - he gets a wage from the company he's working for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Unfortunately, this is an important distinction for Child Benefit eligibility.

I have one more question to make sure I have the full picture: **Are you responsible for Alex, meaning he lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with my determination.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
While you are responsible for Alex and he lives with you, he is currently on a **paid apprenticeship**. Under Child Benefit rules, for children aged 16-19, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if they are in:
- Approved full-time education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to Level 3, etc.), or
- Approved **unpaid** training (such as a traineeship in England)

Because Alex is receiving a wage from his employer as part of his electrician apprenticeship, this counts as **paid employment/training**, which does not qualify for continued Child Benefit.

I'm sorry the outcome wasn't what you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he returns to full-time education), you may wish to revisit your eligibility at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and is on a paid apprenticeship where he receives a wage from his employer. Under Child Benefit rules, you can only claim for a child aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or approved training. A paid apprenticeship does not count as approved education or training for Child Benefit purposes. Approved training includes unpaid traineeships in England, but not paid apprenticeships. Since Alex is receiving a wage for his apprenticeship, he does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit eligibility.
